newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen sells steel works, wire plant.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen sells steel works, wire plant.

text.p: German steel maker Thyssen said on Wednesday that it had signed a declaration of intent to sell its Ruhrort steelworks and its Walzdraht Hochfeld GmbH wire plant to Georgsmarienhuette GmbH.

Thyssen Stahl AG said in a regulatory news release that the sales would enable it to focus on its flat steel business. Thyssen's steel production will fall as a result by 1.5 million tonnes per year and turnover by around 1.0 billion marks ($662.7 million).

Under the agreement, the Ruhrort plant will be demerged from Thyssen Stahl and turned into a separate company and sold along with Walzdraht Hochfeld GmbH, with retroactive effect from October 1 of this year, Thyssen said.
Workers at the two plants will be taken over by Georgsmarienhuette.
Thyssen said that, following supervisory board approval, a legally binding contract would be signed.
